title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Stretch 4 Autodocking

### The Breakthrough
The Open‑source team released an autodocking system for the Stretch 4 robot that uses three retro‑reflective markers detected in LiDAR intensity returns to recover the dock’s 6‑DoF pose via an O(n²) triangle‑leg algorithm. A CUDA‑accelerated MPPI controller builds a 2 m local obstacle map 6× faster than Nav2 and samples thousands of holonomic trajectories per second, achieving docking latencies of 40 ms (CPU) or 65 ms (CPU+GPU). This enables reliable self‑charging in real homes without external infrastructure.

### The Caveats
The demo is limited to videos; no quantitative success rates or baseline comparisons are provided, so reliability versus existing methods is unproven.

## One-Shot LfD for Contact-Rich Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The authors present a one‑shot learning‑from‑demonstration method that extracts physical interaction events from a single demo and uses them as transition triggers for a hybrid position‑force controller. By detecting contact‑based conditions, the controller autonomously switches between position and force modes, handling tasks such as door opening, lock manipulation, bolt picking, and surface contouring on a real robot.

### The Caveats
Only raw success on a handful of tasks is reported, with no baseline comparisons, leaving robustness and the one‑shot advantage unverified.

## Gripper-aware Vision Language Action Models

### The Breakthrough
MiGA, a new dataset of 103 k demonstrations across five robot grippers, fuels GVLA, a vision‑language action model that encodes gripper type via a multi‑gripper tokenizer and adapter‑based policy routing. Experiments in simulation and on real robots show GVLA surpasses existing baselines and improves zero‑shot and few‑shot generalization to new objects and tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper does not name or compare against any existing baselines, so the claimed performance gains lack external validation.

## Fiber Optic Sensing Glove

### The Breakthrough
The glove employs multi‑core shape‑sensing fibers whose full 3‑D shape is reconstructed and registered to a common hand frame; an inverse‑kinematics solver then yields full hand pose at 60 Hz. On a 2‑hour dexterous manipulation dataset it achieves 7.2 mm mean fingertip error, dropping to 4.9 mm after a one‑time factory calibration.

### The Caveats
Accuracy claims are unsubstantiated because the paper provides no comparison to existing sensor or vision‑based hand‑tracking baselines.

## Fiber Bragg Grating Whiskers

### The Breakthrough
Compact FBG whiskers produce a monotonic flow signal from 0.1 to 0.6 µm/s and exhibit far lower self‑induced vibrations than cylindrical baselines; in pitching‑foil tests they detect vortex shedding seconds after passage. Mounted on a miniature robot, a single whisker enabled correct navigation‑branch selection in 17/20 trials (85%).

### The Caveats
Performance is demonstrated only in controlled lab towing and a single robot test; no open‑water or multi‑platform field trials are presented.

## Humanoid Robots Record Claims

### What happened
A Hacker News post claims humanoid robots have outperformed human world‑record times in the 100 m dash, half‑marathon, and high jump, citing advanced actuation, real‑time balance control, and energy‑efficient gait planning as enablers.

### The Caveats
The claim lacks hardware specifications, measurement methodology, and independent verification, so its validity is unsupported.

## nano-ros

### The Breakthrough
nano-ros implements a full ROS 2 stack (pub/sub, services, actions, parameters) in a no_std Rust crate, using zenoh‑pico for lightweight transport and zero‑copy CDR serialization. The build includes formal verification (Kani, CBMC), WCET measurement, and a code‑generation tool that creates Rust bindings from ROS 2 .msg/.srv/.action files, targeting bare‑metal MCUs and RTOSes.

### The Caveats
The library is only demonstrated in QEMU with no real‑hardware performance or latency measurements, leaving its suitability for safety‑critical deployments unproven.

## Geti™

### The Breakthrough
Geti bundles OpenVINO Training Extensions with a UI‑driven app that automates data ingestion, model selection, training, quantization, and deployment, supporting CPU, Intel® XPU, and NVIDIA® CUDA inference. It offers a Python API and out‑of‑the‑box support for classification, detection, and segmentation tasks on edge hardware.

### The Caveats
No benchmark or baseline comparisons are provided, so the claimed edge‑hardware acceleration remains unverified.

### Priority
Stretch 4 autodocking is the most actionable breakthrough today because it delivers a ready‑to‑run, hardware‑level solution for autonomous charging that can be tested on existing home robots.

### One action
Clone the Stretch 4 autodocking repo and run the provided Docker demo to evaluate docking latency on your own robot or simulation.

### What to watch
Multiple papers target high‑fidelity manipulation: the Fiber Optic Glove offers precise hand‑pose capture for data collection, the One‑Shot LfD method focuses on rapid skill transfer from a single demo, and GVLA introduces gripper‑aware language models to generalize across hardware. Together they signal a shift toward more embodied, sensor‑rich pipelines that combine accurate perception with adaptable control.
